decisions.subject: IT Marcello / Comandante Cappellini
decisions.decision: one class with an improved two-boat configuration

urlClassSubjects.subject: Marcello class, including the two later OTO boats

decisions.configurationNote: Marcello migliorata: Comandante Cappellini and Comandante Faà di Bruno, OTO Muggiano, 1938-1939. Regia Marina Italiana's class table places both in class Marcello with the other nine boats. The stated difference from the previous series is Fiat diesels in place of CRDA diesels. That is a series/configuration, not a second served class and not a second required model.

service.event: delivered to the Navy 5 March 1938; first of a stated series of 11
left Cagliari on a war patrol 6 June 1940; left La Spezia 29 September 1940, crossed Gibraltar 5 October, sank Kabalo on the night of 15 October 1940, reached Bordeaux 5 November 1940
delivered to the Regia Marina 23 October 1939; two Mediterranean missions, 10-16 June 1940 and 15-23 July 1940, off Oran
same hull after the armistice; German and Japanese operation stay on this class, not a new design

decisions.subject: FR Aurore / postwar La Créole
decisions.decision: one class; postwar boats are modified completions

urlClassSubjects.subject: classe Aurore, including postwar modified completions

decisions.configurationNote: Only Aurore was finished to the original plans and entered service on 20 June 1940. Five incomplete hulls were completed after the war still inside classe Aurore. La Créole, L'Africaine and L'Astrée are the modified completion (88 mm, 10 tubes, snorkel). L'Andromède and L'Artémise are a further revised configuration with a profiled fin and Narval-trial equipment. German UF2 is the same class.

service.event: enters service 20 June 1940; scuttled at Toulon 27 November 1942
enters service 15 April 1953 to a revised plan
enters service 5 February 1954 to a revised plan
finished by Germany 5 November 1942 and used for training

decisions.subject: DE Type IXD2 / IXD/42, kept apart from IXD1
decisions.decision: IXD/42 is a small-difference variant of IXD2; IXD1 stays a separate machinery type

urlClassSubjects.subject: Type IXD2, including the IXD/42 variant completed as U-883

decisions.configurationNote: U-Boot-Archiv calls IX D42 a variant of the preceding type that 'unterschied sich vom vorhergehenden Typ nur in Kleinigkeiten', same length 87.58 m, same MAN-plus-MWM machinery table, surfaced displacement 1,616 t against 1,610 t for IX D2. Only U 883 was finished. IX D1 is the two-boat Daimler-Benz MB 501 installation, already canonical as type-ixd1-1942. Navypedia's transport heading and stern-tube/252 t cargo line are not adopted as a class.

service.event: commissioned 27 March 1945 as the only IXD/42; training boat of 4. U-Flottille; no patrols; surrendered May 1945; scuttled in Operation Deadlight 31 December 1945
Type IXD1, commissioned 16 May 1942, training flotilla then 12. Flottille active service, two patrols

conflictsUnresolved: Faà di Bruno loss: Regia Marina Italiana says contact was lost and the cause is unknown, and that a postwar HMS Havelock attribution on 8 November 1940 was later doubted because the position was far from the boat's route. uboat.net lists lost 6 November 1940. Navypedia says November 1940, probably Havelock. Service is proved without choosing a loss cause.

Which Marcello boats had Fiat diesels: Regia Marina Italiana limits the previous-series difference to the two later boats. Navypedia's one data block also assigns Fiat diesels to Mocenigo and Veniero. Engine fit is not the class boundary.

Cappellini after the armistice: Regia Marina Italiana says German incorporation as UIT.24 on 10 September 1943. The live German row uses transfer to the Kriegsmarine on 6 December 1943 after Japanese capture. This pass does not replace the December transfer date.
Japanese I-503 date: Regia Marina Italiana says 10 May 1945; the preserved Navypedia UIT24 page says 6 May 1945. Same hull and same class either way.
uboat.net keeps a compiler class named Improved Marcello. That label agrees with the subclass name and disagrees with a second design family. It is not treated as primary proof of a second class.

UF2 end: the same Netmarine thread says destroyed at Gdynia by bombing on 6 July 1944, and a later reply says disarmed 5 July 1944 and scuttled in May 1945. Training service after 5 November 1942 is the served event; the end date stays open.

Postwar Aurore admission years: the Netmarine narrative dates above conflict with Philippe Beriou's coarser year cells and with the Flottes de Combat 1958 column reproduced by Netmarine (La Créole 1946, L'Africaine 1948, L'Astrée 1949). The narrative 'entre en service' dates are the ones used. The 1958 column is not a commissioning date.

U-883 training-flotilla end: uboat.net 5 May 1945 versus U-Boot-Archiv 8 May 1945. Commissioning 27 March 1945 agrees. The archive commander line '27.03.1944' contradicts its own commissioning line and is a typo.

U-Boot-Archiv IX D2/D42 pages say cruising diesels of 5500 PS each and, for D2, both 19.2 kn in the prose and 16.5 kn in the table. Those figures contradict the same pages' machinery lines. They are not used.

IXD/42 as a transport: Navypedia's heading, stern-only tubes and 252 t diesel cargo are not in the U-Boot-Archiv type sheet, which lists four bow and two stern tubes and says the variant differed only in details. Transport completion remains unproved. It would still be a configuration, not a class and not IXD1.

U-Boot-Archiv IX D1 page says the two boats had no torpedo tubes as fuel suppliers and also carries a torpedo count in the data sheet. The Daimler-Benz plant, not that sheet, is what keeps IXD1 distinct.

uboat.net's Type IXD aggregate says 30 commissioned boats and lists IXD1 plus IXD2 through U-876, not U-883. Its own U-883 page still types that boat IXD/42. The 30-boat page is a family count, not a reason to fold IXD1 into IXD2.

Early Project 877 hulls: russianships.info says B-248, B-260 and B-227 were laid down to 877E inside the Project 877 table. Deepstorm lists B-248 as Project 877 with an acceptance act and does not put that 877E note on the boat. Not a separate class.
B-871 entry: Deepstorm boat page, flag 1 December 1990 and in service 30 December 1990. russianships.info says in service 30 November 1990. Late 1990 Soviet naval service is secure; the day is not.

636 versus 877: Admiralty Shipyards says Project 636 was developed from 877 with different equipment and hull rework, and also that Project 636 'является модификацией' of 877 and 877EKM. Deepstorm says 636 was developed from 877EKM for China. This pass keeps the two live canonicals and does not treat the word modification as a completed merge.

Length: Deepstorm gives Project 877 as 72.6 m and the last eight 877 boats as 73.8 m. russianships.info gives Project 636 as 73.8 m and 06363 as 74.5 m. The live China contrast of 72.6 against 73.8 is therefore not a clean 877-versus-636 boundary. 74.5 m is recorded as a 636.3 geometry note, not a third class.
Deepstorm motor line: 5,500 hp on domestic 877 and 4,050 hp on 877EKM, and a 300 m limit noted for EKM against 350 m for the baseline. Engine and depth figures are not a new class.

limits: No Marina Militare official class page, Journal officiel admission decree, Bundesarchiv KTB, or Rubin drawing was retrieved.
CNR INSEAN AMINAVI returned HTTP 503, and the Wayback copy returned HTTP 429. It is not used.
Live Netmarine TLS failed. The classe Aurore thread is a Wayback capture of 18 May 2024, id_ original bytes. The 1958 fleet list is a Wayback capture of 20 February 2003.
Admiralty Shipyards HTTPS failed certificate verification. The cited pages were fetched over HTTP and returned the project text.
U-Boot-Archiv and uboat.net are specialist compilers, independent of Navypedia, not Kriegsmarine originals. The archive cites Busch/Röll and contains the internal numeric errors listed above.
Regia Marina Italiana (regiamarina.net) and sommergibili.com are naval-history sites, not marina.difesa.it. They agree with each other against a second Cappellini class.
Deepstorm is a naval-history compilation and may share books with Navypedia. Acceptance-act sentences are used as service events. They are not the paper acceptance acts.
russianships.info is a compiler, used for the length table and the 877E lay-down conflict.
TASS is a state news report of the flag ceremony. The Admiralty Yakutsk note is the builder's transfer notice.
No live ledger, staged ledger, source tree, asset, or round-18 freeze file was edited. This is not a complete class census.

quotes.quote: The MARCELLO was the first of a series of 11 boats and which bears its name (Marcello Class). The boat was laid down at the C.R.D.A. shipyard of Monfalcone on January 4th, 1937, launched on November 20th of the same year, and delivered to the Navy on March 5th, 1938.
